Pan-Seared Cod with Charred Greens & Brown Butter

Crisp-skinned cod over a bed of fast-charred mustard greens, finished with nutty brown butter, capers, and a squeeze of lemon. A weeknight dinner that punches well above its weight.

Mira Okafor
Published March 14, 2026 Updated April 02, 2026 8 min read
★★★★★ 4.9 · 218 ratings
Prep
10min
Cook
25min
Total
35min
Yield
2servings
Level
Easy

There's a version of fish cookery that scares people off — the dim restaurant kind, with cured citrus and tweezered microgreens. This is not that. This is the version where you stand at the stove with a hot pan and a wedge of lemon and twenty-five minutes later you sit down to dinner. The fish gets crisp. The greens get charred. The butter goes brown. And you eat it on a Tuesday.

The whole thing rests on a single principle: heat, and then leave it alone. Cod is a forgiving fish — denser than you think, sweet, mild, willing — but it asks one thing of you, which is that you not move it. Lay the fillet skin-side down in a cast iron that's hotter than feels reasonable, and then walk away. Set a timer. Pour a glass of something. The skin will release on its own when it's ready, and it will be brown and crackling and the best part of dinner.

The greens here are mustard greens, which I love for their assertive, almost wasabi-like bite — but lacinato kale, broccoli rabe, or even sturdy Swiss chard all work. They get a fast char in the same pan you cooked the fish in, picking up all the fond, all the fishy butter notes, all that good caramelized stuff stuck to the bottom. This is the move. Don't wash the pan between steps. Trust the pan.

The brown butter is two minutes of attention and two minutes only. You'll know it's done when it smells like toasted hazelnuts and your kitchen smells like a French bistro. Pull it the second it goes nut-brown — it goes from gorgeous to acrid in about eleven seconds. A few capers, a squeeze of lemon, done. The acid wakes the whole plate up.

I make this when I want a real dinner without the cognitive load of a real dinner. It's the plate I cook for myself when I get home late, and the plate I cook for someone I want to impress without seeming like I'm trying. (Both situations come up more than you'd think.)

Equipment

  • 10- or 12-inch cast iron skillet
  • Fish spatula (or any thin, flexible spatula)
  • Sharp paring knife
  • Microplane or fine grater
  • Tongs
  • Small bowl for the brown butter
  • Clean kitchen towel (for drying fish)
  • Cutting board

Ingredients

Scale:

For the cod

  • ¾ lb skin-on cod fillets (2 portions, about 6 oz each, at least 1″ thick)
  • 1 tsp kosher salt (Diamond Crystal)
  • ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
  • 2 Tbsp neutral oil (grapeseed or avocado — something with a high smoke point)
  • 1 lemon, halved (for finishing)

For the charred greens

  • 1 lb mustard greens (or lacinato kale, broccoli rabe, or Swiss chard)
  • 3 cloves garlic, thinly sliced
  • ¼ tsp red pepper flakes (or to taste)
  • 1 Tbsp olive oil
  • ¼ cup water or low-sodium chicken stock
  • ½ tsp kosher salt

For the brown butter

  • 4 Tbsp unsalted butter (European-style if you have it)
  • 2 Tbsp capers, drained and patted dry
  • 2 Tbsp flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped
  • 1 tsp lemon zest (from the lemon above)
  • flaky sea salt, to finish (Maldon or similar)

Instructions

Total: 35 min
  1. Prep · 10 min

    Pull the cod from the fridge 15 minutes before cooking — cold fish hits a hot pan and seizes. While it tempers, wash and stem the mustard greens, tearing larger leaves into 4–5 inch pieces. Slice the garlic. Zest the lemon, then halve it. Pat the cod fillets very dry on both sides with a clean towel — this is non-negotiable for crisp skin.

  2. Sear · 6 min

    Heat your cast iron over medium-high until it's smoking faintly — about 3 minutes. Add the neutral oil and swirl. Season the fillets generously with kosher salt and pepper on the flesh side only. Lay them in the pan skin-side down, pressing gently with a spatula for the first 10 seconds so the skin makes full contact and doesn't curl. Then leave them alone. Truly alone. Set a timer.

  3. Don't touch · 4 min

    After 4 minutes, peek under one fillet with the spatula. The skin should be deep golden-brown and release cleanly from the pan. If it sticks, give it another 30 seconds. Flip carefully and cook 60–90 seconds more on the flesh side, just until the cod is opaque and flakes when pressed. Transfer to a plate, skin-side up, and tent loosely with foil.

  4. Char the greens · 5 min

    Without wiping the pan, return it to medium-high heat. Add the olive oil, then dump in the mustard greens — they'll sputter. Spread them in a single layer and press them down with tongs. Don't stir. Let them char in spots for about 90 seconds, then toss once and let them char again for another minute.

  5. Build flavor · 2 min

    Push the greens to one side. Add the garlic and red pepper flakes to the cleared space and stir for 30 seconds, just until fragrant — don't let the garlic brown or it'll turn bitter. Pour in the water or stock, scraping up any browned bits with a wooden spoon, then toss everything together. Add the ½ teaspoon salt, taste, and adjust. The greens should be wilted but still have a little bite. Slide them onto two warmed plates.

  6. Brown the butter · 3 min

    Wipe the skillet with a paper towel and return it to medium heat. Add the butter. It will melt, then foam, then quiet down, then start to smell like toasted hazelnuts — that's your cue. Swirl the pan constantly once you see brown specks forming on the bottom. Pull it from the heat the instant it's deep golden — about 2 minutes total. Off-heat, drop in the capers (carefully, they'll sputter) and let them sizzle for 20 seconds.

  7. Finish · 1 min

    Stir the parsley and lemon zest into the brown butter. Lay the cod fillets, skin-side up, on top of the charred greens. Spoon the brown butter, capers and all, generously over and around the fish. Squeeze half the lemon over everything. Finish with a pinch of flaky salt.

  8. Serve · now

    Eat immediately — the skin is at peak crispness for about 90 seconds. A piece of charred bread on the side is not optional in my house, but you do you. Reserve the remaining lemon half for the table.

Mira's notes & make-ahead

On the fish: Skin-on, please. Skinless cod will work but you'll lose the best part of the dish. Frozen cod is fine — most "fresh" cod at supermarkets was frozen anyway — just thaw it slowly in the fridge overnight and dry it within an inch of its life.

On the pan: Cast iron is genuinely the right tool here. A nonstick won't get hot enough for proper skin crisping, and stainless requires more oil and more nerve. If you only have nonstick, crank the heat higher than you think and accept that the skin will be less shattery.

Make-ahead: You can wash and tear the greens up to 2 days ahead — store in a paper-towel-lined bag in the crisper. Slice the garlic and zest the lemon up to 24 hours ahead. The brown butter is best made à la minute and does not reheat well.

Storage: Leftover cod is sad. If you must, flake it into a green salad with capers the next day for lunch — call it composed and forget it was ever a hot dinner.

Substitutions

Swaps that won't compromise the dish
Original Substitute Notes
Cod Haddock, pollock, hake, halibut, or arctic char Any firm, white, mild fish. Cook time stays the same per inch of thickness.
Mustard greens Lacinato kale, broccoli rabe, dandelion, Swiss chard Tougher greens (kale, rabe) need 1–2 extra minutes; chard cooks faster.
Capers Chopped Castelvetrano olives or pickled mustard seeds Both bring brine and pop without the same punchy bitterness.
Brown butter Olive oil heated with anchovies until they melt A different dish, technically, but in the same emotional family.
Lemon Meyer lemon or a splash of white wine vinegar Meyer is sweeter — use a touch more. Vinegar: about 1 teaspoon.
